## Goal
Remove the now-unused `'onImpact'` AOE projectile-detonation machinery (dead code retained by AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9) and its tests, now that no catalogue weapon uses the `'onImpact'` trigger.

## Context
AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9 moved the Mortar from `'onImpact'` to `'onRandom'`, so the `'onImpact'` path is no longer referenced by any weapon definition. Per project dead-code discipline it was deliberately retained during that change; this item is the follow-up cleanup (discovered-from:AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9).

## Scope (in)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts`: drop `'onImpact'` from the `AoETrigger` union; remove the `onImpact` descriptor doc; remove `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` if it has no remaining consumer (the Mortar's range basis is to be made explicit separately if needed).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`: remove the `onAoeProjectileSpawned` hook and the `'onImpact'` branch in `_autoFire` (bullet spawn is then only unreachable; decide whether projectile spawn remains for any weapon).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`, `detonateAoeProjectile`, the `bullet.aoeWeapon` handling in `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`, and the mortar VFX/sound path from `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` if unused.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`: remove `aoeWeapon`, `aoeDetonated`, `onExpire` (if only used by the AOE path) and their comments.
- `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`: remove the retained `onImpact` tests (the section marked 'Retained onImpact projectile-detonation machinery (dead code)').
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`/`detonateAoeProjectile` from `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`: update the descriptor union text (remove `'onImpact'`) and any remaining onImpact references.

## Out of scope
- Any behavioural change to Nova, Mortar or Arc.
- Removing the generic player-bullet spawn path used by conventional weapons.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 — `AoETrigger` is `'onFire' | 'onRandom'`; no source references `'onImpact'` remain (except historical docs/changelog if intentionally kept — enumerate any).
- [ ] AC2 — The onImpact hooks/methods and `PlayerBullet` AOE fields are removed, and `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- [ ] AC3 — The retained-onImpact tests are removed; `AoeWeapons.test.ts` still covers Nova/Arc/Mortar random detonation.
- [ ] AC4 — Gym↔game parity guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still passes with the reduced `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- [ ] AC5 — Docs (`docs/Game Design Document.md`) still pass `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` (or are updated if the guard references removed strings).
- [ ] AC6 — Full suite green (`/skill:test`).

## Notes / risks
- `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` (Mortar burst + cue, off-screen culling) is still needed by the `'onRandom'` path — do not remove it.
- The generic `spawnPlayerBullet` path must remain for the cannon/spread/dual/rapid.
- If any consumer of `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` remains as the Mortar range basis, either keep it (renamed/documented) or replace the range basis explicitly; do not silently drop the Mortar range.
data.title: Remove the onImpact projectile-detonation machinery and its tests

# Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code
`bulletSpeed: 200` for **unknown** archetype keys and were explicitly out of that
item's scope (its Q2 enumeration covered only CSV + defaults + entity constants):

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of
every shipped archetype, so tuning can still drift for that edge case.

## Desired change

Decide and, if accepted, halve these three `bulletSpeed` fallbacks (200 → 100) for
consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — The three unknown-archetype fallbacks use `bulletSpeed: 100` (or a
  documented decision is recorded to leave them at 200 with rationale).
- [ ] AC2 — Any difficulty-sequencer or difficulty-scoring test affected by the
  change is updated and the full suite passes.
- [ ] AC3 — The decision and rationale are recorded on this item.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`

## Related work

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent discovery; strictly out of its scope).

discovered-from:AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A

## Problem

Several deterministic bot micro-simulations are knife-edge calibrations: a subtle, legitimate gameplay tweak (e.g. the 1-5% gentler thrust-press reduction in AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A) flips their outcomes because scores are dominated by discrete hit/bullet collisions.

During AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A two tests had to be recalibrated:
- src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts - synthetic human seed moved 7 -> 14.
- src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts - RUN_SEED moved 0x0b07 -> 0x0b16.

On the base behaviour, src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts already regressed on 13/24 seeds, and the competent-vs-legacy AC6 test only wins in base because the legacy bot chaotically collides with bullets; without bullets the legacy bot scored higher (22 vs 20) on base.

## Goal

Make these tests robust rather than seed-picked:
- Aggregate competence/style comparisons over a set of seeds (e.g. assert the styled/competent bot is not systematically worse), or
- Compare on scenarios whose score is not dominated by discrete collisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The style-match AC4 demonstration no longer depends on a single lucky seed (e.g. asserts over multiple seeds).
- AC2: The competent-vs-legacy AC6 test asserts an objective-based advantage rather than relying on chaotic bullet collisions.
- AC3: Recalibrating either test is not required by an unrelated small bot-feel tweak.
- AC4: Full test suite, typecheck and build pass.
data.title: Make bot micro-simulation tests robust to small feel tweaks

# New flag is more noticeable (AH-0MVCFH6I4000AWRI)

## Problem statement

On the hold-full ("HULL FULL — CHOOSE A POWER-UP") reward overlay the `★ New`
marker for an item the player does not yet own is rendered as a small (14 px),
muted-orange detail line **beneath** the option's description, where it reads as
just another piece of detail copy. With three options on screen, a reduced-volume
ghost fire running and a 3-2-1 countdown competing for attention, players miss the
marker and read a brand-new item as an upgrade to something they already own.

## Users

- **Player (at-a-glance scan):** "As a player whose hold has just filled, I want
  brand-new offers to jump out of the list immediately, so I can tell 'this is
  something I don't own yet' from 'this is an upgrade' without reading every
  line."
- **Player (reward readability):** "As a player I want the New marker attached to
  the item's title so I cannot lose it in the description/countdown noise."
- **Designer / tuner:** "As a designer I want the emphasis produced by a single
  shared overlay implementation, so the game and every gym show the same
  presentation and the tuning lives in one place."

## Current behaviour (existing state)

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` renders each option as a three-line block:
  1. title line `${index + 1}.  ${option.name}` — 20 px, cyan `#00ffff`,
     centred at `GAME_WIDTH / 2`, with `#111111` background padding;
  2. description line (13 px, `#cccccc`) at `y + 28`;
  3. detail line (14 px) at `y + 48` — the change summary
     (e.g. `+1 Projectiles`) or the string `★ New` in orange `#ff8800`
     (`CHOICE_NEW_COLOR`). `New` takes display priority over a change summary.
- The badge is static: no weight, no motion, no glow. Its container
  `getDetailLines()` is what the scene tests assert against.
- Existing agreed behaviour: **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR · AC4** specifies the badge as
  "a second, smaller detail line beneath the option name" and the three-line
  block is documented in the Game Design Document §4.5 and the README module
  entry for the overlay. Those two statements are what this item deliberately
  revises.
- Existing tests that pin the current presentation:
  `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` —
  `renders a "New" badge for options marked isNew` (asserts
  `getDetailLines()[0] === '★ New'`), `"New" badge takes display priority over
  changeSummary`, and `AC2 — shows a New option's description above its ★ New
  badge`.

## Desired change

1. Move the `★ New` marker to the **start of the title line**, ahead of the
   numbered name, so it is visually part of the item's heading.
2. Make it **bolder**: bold weight, larger than the current 14 px detail text,
   high-contrast treatment (stroke and/or text shadow) so it reads from a
   distance.
3. Give it **motion and light**: a continuous pulse (scale/alpha) plus a visible
   glow that intensifies with the pulse.
4. Stop repeating the marker on the detail line — the detail line keeps only the
   change summary (see Q2 below; the draft assumes removal).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Badge leads the title line.** For every option with `isNew`, the
  presetation renders the `★ New` marker on the **same row as the option title
  and to the left of that title** (reading order `★ New` → `1.` → item name), on
  the title line's vertical centre. Options without `isNew` render no marker.
- **AC2 — Bolder than before.** The marker is rendered in a bold weight with a
  font size strictly larger than the previous 14 px detail text, plus a visible
  stroke or text shadow, at a contrast that is at least as strong as the current
  `#ff8800` orange against the `#000000` backdrop.
- **AC3 — Pulses.** The marker animates continuously while the overlay is open
  with a yoyo tween over bounded properties (scale and/or alpha), period within
  600–1200 ms, scale amplitude ≤ 1.15 and alpha floor ≥ 0.6, so it stays inside
  its row (row pitch is 84 px) and never touches the title text or the
  neighbouring rows.
- **AC4 — Glows.** A visible glow accompanies the pulse (text shadow with blur
  and/or stroke) whose intensity is animated in step with AC3, remaining legible
  at every phase of the pulse.
- **AC5 — No duplicate marker, no layout regression.** The detail line no longer
  contains `★ New` (producer Q2 = A, revising AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR · AC4); change
  summaries continue to render beneath the description;
  `getOptionLabels()` still contains the option number and name; the existing
  three-line block (title → description → detail) and row pitch are preserved.
- **AC6 — Clean teardown.** Every pulse/glow tween is stopped and the marker
  objects destroyed when the selection countdown starts
  (`AH-0MV722WJS0075UTZ` teardown path) and when the scene shuts down — no
  orphaned tweens or tweens targeting destroyed text.
- **AC7 — Gym↔game parity.** The change lives once in the shared overlay
  (`MineralChoiceScene`), so `PlayScene` and every gym that opens it present the
  identical marker; no divergent copy is introduced.
- **AC8 — Testing/validation.** Scene tests cover: marker present at the title
  line start for `isNew` options and absent otherwise; bold/larger style
  asserted; pulse tween exists with the expected target properties and is
  removed on teardown; detail line no longer carries `★ New` while change
  summaries still render. Each test asserts a behaviour, not internal constants.
- **AC9 — Documentation.** Game Design Document §4.5 and the README
  `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` entry describe the title-line marker with
  its pulse/glow, and the code comments in the scene are updated. (CHANGELOG is
  handled by the release pipeline and is out of scope.)
- **AC10 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope).

## Constraints

- **Single shared implementation.** `MineralChoiceScene` is consumed by
  `PlayScene` and every gym (`GymFormationScene`, `GymWeaponLeveling`, …); the
  marker is implemented once there. No per-launcher option or flag.
- **Phaser 4 text only.** No new sprites or binary assets; the glow is achieved
  with Phaser text styling (`stroke`, `shadow`) and tweens.
- **Demo/attract mode safe.** The demo launcher auto-selects after a delay
  (`autoSelectMs`). The pulse must not delay, block or interfere with selection,
  the 3-2-1 countdown, or the ghost-fire metronome.
- **No new settings surface.** There is no reduced-motion setting in
  `configStore` today; this item does not add one (bounded amplitude keeps the
  motion mild). If the producer wants a visibility/reduce-motion toggle, that is
  a separate item.
- **Headless eval unaffected.** The perception-free eval arena never opens the
  overlay, so no eval-parity work is required; the existing parity tests keep
  guarding shared behaviour.

## Existing state / Desired change summary

| Aspect | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| Position | detail line under the description (`y + 48`) | start of the title line, left of `1.  <name>` |
| Weight | regular 14 px | bold, larger than 14 px, stroked/shadowed |
| Motion | none | continuous bounded pulse + glow |
| Detail line | `★ New` or change summary | change summary only |

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — add the title-line marker text object,
  style constants (size/colour/stroke/shadow), pulse/glow tween creation and
  teardown, plus a test accessor (e.g. `getNewBadges()` returning the marker
  texts/tweens) alongside the existing `getOptionLabels()` / `getDetailLines()`
  accessors.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — revise the three existing
  `New` badge assertions to the new contract and add placement, style, tween and
  teardown coverage.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.5 hold-full choice overlay bullet: marker
  presentation (title-line start, bold, pulsing, glowing).
- `README.md` — `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` module entry: same
  description in the three-line block summary.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR** (completed) — introduced the change summary and the
  `★ New` badge as a detail line; AC4 is the statement this item revises.
- **AH-0MV2N2591007UGPD** (completed) — added the description line and the
  three-line block that positions the marker today.
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** (completed) — created the shared hold-full overlay and
  its zero-launcher-knowledge contract.
- **AH-0MV722WJS0075UTZ** (completed) — countdown + teardown path the pulse must
  respect.
- **AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9** (completed) — power-up levelling, which made the badge
  apply to power-ups as well as weapons (so up to three markers can be on screen
  at once).
- **AH-0MVCFB00Y004AQ2Z** (completed) — sibling hold-full-screen item, same area
  of the overlay (recent precedent for intake → implement on this screen).

## Assumptions (A1–A2 confirmed by the producer; A3–A5 are implementation defaults)

- **A1.** The marker text stays `★ New` (uppercase-initial, star prefix) rather
  than becoming `NEW` / `NEW!`; only its weight, size, position, motion and glow
  change. Rationale: it keeps the wording players have seen and keeps the
  existing string assertions meaningful.
- **A2.** The base colour stays the orange `CHOICE_NEW_COLOR` (`#ff8800`); the
  glow adds light (white/amber shadow) rather than changing the hue.
- **A3.** The pulse runs continuously for as long as the overlay is open (one
  tween per marker), rather than pulsing a fixed number of times.
- **A4.** Marker motion is implemented per-marker with the same tween
  configuration; no per-index phase offset (three markers pulsing in step is
  acceptable).
- **A5.** The marker does not change the overlay's width, centring rules or the
  row pitch; the title line is laid out as `[marker][gap][numbered name]` with
  both anchored relative to the existing centred title.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

> Recorded via `/skill:intake`. All three interview questions were answered by
> the producer (2026-10-25, interactive reply), each with the recommended option
> **A**; no open questions remain.

- **Q1 — Does the marker become a separate object beside the title, or become
  part of the title string?**
  Options: **(A)** a separate text object anchored to the left of the existing
  title text, leaving `getOptionLabels()` unchanged; **(B)** prefix the title
  string (`★ New  1.  Spread Shot`).
  **Recommended:** A — keeps the tested label contract and centring intact and
  gives the marker its own tween target.
  Answer (producer, 2026-10-25, interactive reply): **A** — a separate marker
  object; `getOptionLabels()` stays unchanged.

- **Q2 — Should the `★ New` marker remain on the detail line as well?**
  Options: **(A)** remove it from the detail line (marker now lives on the title
  line; upgrades keep their summary line); **(B)** keep both (duplicate marker,
  maximum visibility but redundant); **(C)** keep the detail line unchanged and
  simply add the emphasised marker to the title as well.
  **Recommended:** A — a single marker is clearer, and duplicating `★ New` in two
  places would fight the countdown for attention.
  Answer (producer, 2026-10-25, interactive reply): **A** — remove the marker
  from the detail line; this supersedes AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR · AC4 ("second,
  smaller detail line") and the three-line-block wording in GDD §4.5 and the
  README module entry.

- **Q3 — How strong should the motion be, and does it need an accessibility
  opt-out?**
  Options: **(A)** continuous subtle pulse (alpha 0.75↔1.0, scale 1.0↔1.08,
  ~700 ms yoyo) with a matching glow, always on; **(B)** pulse three times on
  open, then settle into a static glow; **(C)** continuous pulse plus a new
  reduce-motion/visibility toggle in settings.
  **Recommended:** A — clearly noticeable while staying inside the 84 px row and
  adding no new settings surface; C would be a separate item.
  Answer (producer, 2026-10-25, interactive reply): **A** — continuous subtle
  pulse (alpha 0.75↔1.0, scale 1.0↔1.08, ~700 ms yoyo) with a matching glow,
  always on; no reduce-motion setting in this item.

- **Q4 — Where is the marker tuned?** Research: no repository or work-item answer
  needed — the repo has no motion/flash setting in `configStore`
  (`src/core/configTypes.ts`), and overlay styling constants live at the top of
  `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` (`CHOICE_NEW_COLOR`, `CHOICE_ROW_PITCH`,
  …). Resolution: all new marker constants are module-level named constants in
  the same block, matching the existing convention (mirrors
  AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR · AC3 "single source of truth"). Source: repo inspection
  of `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` and `src/core/configTypes.ts`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR** – Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list (completed)
- **AH-0MUDYTM7C00071Y1** – Change the current mineral count to a bar that fills (completed)
- **AH-0MVDV560Z002PSLT** – Full project test suite passes with the new changes (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 00ffff, 0mubvgi62004ed9q, 0muu1goau007rfvr, 0muv5clvo002zhs9, 0mv2n2591007ugpd (+397 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0muv5clvo002zhs9, 0mv2n2591007ugpd, 0mvcfb00y004aq2z, absent, ac1 (+387 more)

# On the hull-full upgrade screen show current upgrades

**Headline:** Add a permanent-only "currently owned upgrades/weapons" panel to the top-left of the hold-full choice overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`), derived from the run's permanent weapon and power-up levels so a temporary field pickup can never appear in it or inflate a displayed level.

## Original request (verbatim)

> When the player is offered a hull full upgrade they are given a list of three items, ones that are new are labelled, ones that are upgrades show the upgrade parameters. We also need to list (in the top left) the currently owned upgrades/weapons. This list should not include temporary, only permanent upgrades. If they show a level they should show only the permanent level not any temporary level upgrades.

> **Terminology:** the request says "hull full"; the shipped feature is the **hold-full choice** overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`, GDD §4.4.1), opened when the mineral hold fills. This brief treats "hull-full" as "hold-full", consistent with AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR and AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF.

## Problem statement

The hold-full choice now shows each offered item's name, a one-line description and (for levelled offers) a level-accurate change summary, plus a `★ New` badge for items the player does not own (AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR, AH-0MV2N2591007UGPD, AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON). What the screen still hides is the **other half of the picture**: the build the player already has. A player offered "Spread Shot Lv.3" cannot see whether they own Rapid Fire Lv.4 or a Shield, so a levelled choice is made blind. The overlay is also the only moment where gameplay is paused and a permanent decision is taken, so it is the natural place to show the current permanent loadout.

## Users

- **Player (informed build choice):** "As a player, when the hold fills, I want to see everything I already own permanently — weapons and power-ups, with their permanent levels — so I can judge whether a new offer fits my build."
- **Player (no mental arithmetic):** "As a player, I don't want my displayed level to include a 10-second field pickup I happened to catch, because the permanent level is what the offer is priced against."
- **Designer/tuner:** "As a designer, I want the list derived from the same permanent-only snapshots the choice pool already uses, so the panel can never disagree with what is offered."

### Example user stories

- As a player with `Spread Shot Lv.2`, `Rapid Fire Lv.1` and `Shield Lv.3` permanently owned, I see those three listed top-left when the hold fills.
- As a player who caught a field `Spread Shot` five seconds ago (temporary stack only, no permanent grant), the panel does **not** list Spread Shot, and if I own `Rapid Fire Lv.1` the panel shows `Lv.1`, not `Lv.2`.
- As a player opening the very first hold-full choice of a run, the panel tells me plainly that I own nothing permanent yet.

## Acceptance Criteria

> The three presentation decisions were confirmed by the producer during intake (Q1 = A, Q2 = A, Q3 = A; see the Appendix).

- **AC1 — Owned permanent items are listed.** The hold-full overlay renders, in the top-left of the screen, every item the player owns **permanently** this run — permanent **weapons and power-ups** — as one row per item. The permanent `cannon` is excluded (it is the base weapon, never a permanent reward) and so is the `reset` utility.
- **AC2 — Permanent only.** Temporary (field-pickup) upgrades never appear in the panel, and a displayed level is the item's **permanent level only** (`getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()`), never `permanent + temporary`. A field-only item is absent from the panel and still offered as `★ New`.
- **AC3 — Single source of truth.** The panel's item names come from the shared choice/catalogue naming (`toChoiceOption(id).name` in `src/powerups/choice.ts`, itself backed by `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` / `WEAPON_NAMES`); no second name table or duplicated level arithmetic is introduced in the scene.
- **AC4 — Level display.** Every row always shows the item's permanent level as `Lv.N`, including `Lv.1` (e.g. `Spread Shot Lv.2`, `Shield Lv.3`, `Rapid Fire Lv.1`), matching the offer labels on the same screen so a level-1 item and a levelled item are unambiguously distinguishable.
- **AC5 — Presentation & empty state.** The panel is a **single flat list** under the heading `YOUR UPGRADES`, rendered top-left (weapons first, then power-ups, catalogue order within each kind, so the order is deterministic). When the player owns nothing permanently, the heading reads `YOUR UPGRADES — none yet` rather than an empty/blank region. The panel must not collide with the centred option column (3 options, `CHOICE_FIRST_ROW_Y`…`+ pitch × 2`) at the shipped game resolution.
- **AC6 — Gym↔game parity.** Every launcher that opens the hold-full choice (`PlayScene.openMineralChoice`, `GymFormationScene.openMineralChoice`, `GymWeaponLeveling.openMineralChoice`, `GymPowerUpLeveling.openMineralChoice`) supplies the same permanent snapshots it already passes to the strategy context, so the panel behaves identically in the game and every gym; no divergent copy.
- **AC7 — Teardown & lifecycle.** The panel is destroyed with the rest of the choice UI when a selection starts the 3-2-1 countdown, and is rebuilt from current state the next time the overlay opens (no stale carry-over between hold-full events).
- **AC8 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests cover the pure owned-loadout builder (permanent-only filtering, cannon/`reset` exclusion, deterministic ordering, `Lv.N` labels, empty case) and scene tests cover the rendered rows, the empty state, the teardown, and that a temporary-only weapon/power-up never appears and never raises a displayed level. Every test asserts a meaningful behaviour (TDD preferred).
- **AC9 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README (where the overlay is described) and GDD §4.4.1 (hold-full choice presentation).
- **AC10 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** behaviour lives once — a pure builder consumed through the launcher payload, rendered by the single shared `MineralChoiceScene`; the duplicate-body guard and gym-parity docs assertion must stay green.
- **Backward compatibility:** the overlay's `init` payload gains an **optional** field; isolated scene tests that launch it with `options` only must keep working (absence → panel omitted or empty state, decided by the implementation and covered by a test).
- **No live mutation:** the panel reflects the permanent snapshots captured at launch; it need not update while the overlay is open (the choice is applied after the countdown, at which point the overlay closes).
- **Do not change the offered options, their order, the change summaries, the `★ New` badge, or the 3-offer mechanism** — this item is additive presentation.
- **Keep the existing accessors intact:** `getOptionLabels()`, `getDetailLines()`, `getDescriptionLines()` assertions must not break; add a new accessor for the panel rows.
- **Bounded list:** the six-slot permanent cap (AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF, `src/powerups/slots.ts`) bounds the list to ≤ 6 kinds plus any `availableWhenSlotsFull` exemptions, so no scrolling/paging design is required.
- **Run-scoped only:** no leaderboard or persistence impact.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — modal overlay: opaque backdrop, `HOLD FULL — CHOOSE A POWER-UP` heading at `y = 120`, one centred option block every `CHOICE_ROW_PITCH = 84` px from `CHOICE_FIRST_ROW_Y = 200` (name → description → change summary/`★ New`); `getOptionLabels()` / `getDetailLines()` / `getDescriptionLines()`; `_teardownChoiceUi()` destroys backdrop, heading, controls, detail/description lines and the keydown listener when the countdown starts.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `openMineralChoice()` — already computes `weaponLevels: player.getWeaponLevels()` and `powerUpLevels: player.getPowerUpLevels()` for the strategy context, but passes only `options`, `fireSchedule`, demo auto-select params and `onSelect` to `scene.launch('MineralChoiceScene', …)`.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — same pattern (compute the two snapshots, pass options + `fireSchedule` + `onSelect`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `openMiniBossReward()` — also launches `MineralChoiceScene`, with `buildUpgradeOptions({ weaponLevels, powerUpLevels })`; **no** owned panel supplied today (see Risks).
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `ChoiceOption`, `toChoiceOption(id)` (name + description from the shared catalogues), `WEAPON_NAMES`, `buildLevelUpOption`, `buildOwnedLevelUpOptions`.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — `resolveSlotState(powerUpLevels, weaponLevels)` → `{ used, free, isFull, ownedIds }`; already filters the permanent `cannon` and derives occupancy from the two **permanent-only** snapshots.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `getWeaponLevels()` (permanent weapon grants only) and `getPowerUpLevels()` → `PowerUpLevelStore.getLevels()` (permanent power-up grants only).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — existing owned-item row label convention `"<Name> Lvl <N>"` for the in-run HUD rows.
- GDD §4.4.1 documents the hold-full choice overlay, its option copy and the change-summary/`★ New` contract; its **Permanent pick** bullet names only `PlayScene`, `GymFormationScene` and `GymWeaponLeveling` as launchers.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — the hold-full launcher parity guard ("every launcher passes the common overlay payload", `HOLDFULL_LAUNCHERS`) lists only `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` and `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`; `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` also launches the overlay but is **absent** from that list.
- `src/choiceDescriptionsDocs.test.ts` — the existing §4.4.1 docs guard (overlay option copy); `src/powerUpSlotsDocs.test.ts` holds the same `holdFullChoiceSection()` helper pattern.

## Desired change

1. **Pure owned-loadout builder (new module, e.g. `src/powerups/ownedLoadout.ts`)** — `buildOwnedLoadout(powerUpLevels, weaponLevels)` returning the permanent loadout as display rows (`{ id, kind, name, level, label }`), ordered deterministically (weapons first, then power-ups, catalogue order within each kind), each labelled `"<Name> Lv.<N>"`. Filters non-drop ids (`cannon`, `reset`) via the existing `isWeaponDrop` guard and names rows through `toChoiceOption(id).name`, so naming stays single-sourced.
2. **Overlay payload** — `MineralChoiceScene.init` accepts the built rows (optional); `create()` renders them top-left as the `YOUR UPGRADES` heading plus one `Lv.N` row per item (and the `YOUR UPGRADES — none yet` empty state), stored for teardown and exposed via a new test accessor (e.g. `getOwnedUpgradeLines()`); `_teardownChoiceUi()` destroys them.
3. **Launchers** — each hold-full launcher passes the rows built from the **same** `getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` snapshots it already gathers for the strategy, so the panel and the offers can never disagree. `GymPowerUpLeveling` currently passes **only** `powerUpLevels` to the strategy context, so it adds a `this.player?.getWeaponLevels() ?? []` read for the panel rows (a read of the same permanent snapshot, not new state); its offer pool stays power-ups-only. See the Open Question below.
4. **Tests and documentation** — as per AC8/AC9: builder unit tests plus scene assertions for the panel rows, empty state, teardown and temporary-level exclusion; extend the **hold-full launcher parity guard** (add `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` to `HOLDFULL_LAUNCHERS` and assert every launcher passes the owned rows); add launcher-level assertions that each hold-full scene forwards the rows; update GDD §4.4.1 (panel, permanent-only rule, and the launcher list that omits `GymPowerUpLeveling`) and extend the §4.4.1 docs guard in `src/choiceDescriptionsDocs.test.ts` so the panel copy cannot silently drift.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/ownedLoadout.ts` *(new)* — pure permanent-loadout builder; filters non-drop ids, names via `toChoiceOption`, formats the level label.
- `src/powerups/ownedLoadout.test.ts` *(new)* — permanent-only filtering, ordering, labels, empty case, temporary-only exclusion.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — top-left panel rendering, empty state, teardown, `getOwnedUpgradeLines()`.
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — panel rows/empty state/teardown/temporary-exclusion assertions.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — pass the built rows to the overlay launch payload.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend `HOLDFULL_LAUNCHERS` with `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` and assert every launcher passes the owned-loadout rows (AC6 · gym↔game parity).
- `src/scenes/__tests__/PlayScene.minerals.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — launcher-level assertions that the overlay receives the built rows (AC6).
- `src/choiceDescriptionsDocs.test.ts` — extend the §4.4.1 docs guard with the `YOUR UPGRADES` panel and its permanent-only rule (AC9).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.1 — document the owned-permanents panel and its permanent-only rule; correct the launcher list in the **Permanent pick** bullet to include `GymPowerUpLeveling`.
- `README.md` — feature pointer if the overlay's capabilities are listed there.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR** — Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list (completed): built the option `changeSummary` / `★ New` detail line this panel sits beside.
- **AH-0MV2N2591007UGPD** — Upgrade and weapon descriptions (completed): added the description line and the shared catalogue copy the panel reuses.
- **AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON** — Upgrade text must reflect the actual upgrade (completed): level-accurate summaries from the permanent level.
- **AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF** — Limit the number of powerup slots (in progress): the six-slot permanent cap bounds this list to ≤ 6 kinds; `resolveSlotState` uses the same permanent-only snapshots.
- **AH-0MUX802450085VZZ / AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9 / AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K** — Permanent vs temporary split for weapons and power-ups, and the single `PowerUpLevelStore` the panel reads.
- **AH-0MU7JTEY3004EXR2** — Show level/wave progress as 'Level N of 5, Wave M of K' (completed): the existing top-left HUD readout, hidden behind the overlay's opaque backdrop.
- **AH-0MU7JTFY1006QA8I** — HUD lives label overlapped by active power-ups list (completed): precedent for owned-item list layout care.
- GDD §4.4.1 (hold-full choice), §4.4.2 (weapon leveling), §4.4.3 (power-up leveling).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep (medium):** "show current upgrades" can drift into redesigning the overlay. Mitigation: additive panel only; no change to offers, ordering, summaries or badges. Further presentation ideas become linked work items.
- **Mini-boss reward overlay (medium):** `openMiniBossReward()` reuses `MineralChoiceScene` but is not the "hull-full" screen. Default (recorded non-blocking during intake, no objection raised): the panel is supplied by the **hold-full** launchers only; adding it to the mini-boss reward is a separate, cheap follow-up if wanted.
- **Layout collision (low):** option descriptions are wide, centred text; a top-left panel must stay clear of them at the shipped resolution. Verified by a scene test asserting the panel's anchor and by manual gym check.
- **Temporary-level leakage (low):** `getWeaponLevels()` / `getPowerUpLevels()` are already permanent-only, but the panel must not be tempted to read `getWeaponLevel()` / `getPowerUpLevel()` (effective levels). Guarded by a test that adds a temporary stack and asserts the displayed level is unchanged.
- **Name drift (low):** mitigated by resolving every row name through `toChoiceOption` rather than a new table.
- **Test coupling (low):** existing label/detail/description accessor assertions must keep passing — the panel is a separate set of game objects.
- **Assumption:** "hull full" = the hold-full mineral choice overlay (the only permanent-choice list), consistent with the sibling items.

## Open questions (plan review)

- **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking) — weapons panel in `GymPowerUpLeveling`.** That gym passes only `powerUpLevels` (no `weaponLevels`) to the choice strategy context, so AC1 ("every permanently-owned weapon **and** power-up") and AC6 ("the same permanent snapshots it already passes to the strategy context") disagree there. **Default recorded for implementation:** build the panel from `getWeaponLevels()` + `getPowerUpLevels()` in every launcher, including `GymPowerUpLeveling`, so the panel always states the run's true permanent loadout; that gym's offer pool stays power-ups-only and the panel does not change it. Directed to: producer (confirm or overrule the default) — it only matters if the panel must mirror a gym's disabled weapon offers instead of the run's actual loadout.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-28 — `plan` skill, auto-complete path** (pre-check: effort Small / risk Low). Six review stages run on the existing intake brief; changes kept conservative and additive: Existing state records the stale parity-guard launcher list and the existing §4.4.1 docs guard; Desired change steps 3–4 make the panel's snapshot source, the parity-guard extension and the docs-guard update explicit; Key Files gains the parity guard, the four launcher tests and the docs guard; one non-blocking Open Question records the `GymPowerUpLeveling` weapon-snapshot default. No acceptance criteria changed; no children created (one small vertical slice, no phasing needed).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded during intake for AH-0MVCRKAPL000L68Y (operator = Producer). Research performed before asking: read `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts`, `src/powerups/choice.ts`, `src/powerups/slots.ts`, `src/entities/Player.ts`, `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, `src/ui/HUD.ts`, the four hold-full launchers, GDD §4.4.1–§4.4.3, and worklog items AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR, AH-0MV2N2591007UGPD, AH-0MVL9P2SF009QFON, AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF. All three questions were asked together (one round, multiple-choice with a stated recommendation) and answered in one reply.

- **Q1 — Content scope: which owned items appear in the top-left list?**
  - A: Every permanently-owned power-up **and** weapon drop (the permanent cannon excluded, field-only/temporary items excluded). — **Recommended:** simplest reading of the request, and matches the shared six-slot loadout that the choice pool already prices.
  - B: Weapons only.
  - C: Power-ups only.
  - **Answer (Producer, interactive reply):** **A** — every permanently-owned power-up and weapon drop; the cannon and field-only/temporary items are excluded.
  - **Research:** `Player.getWeaponLevels()` and `PowerUpLevelStore.getLevels()` both return permanent grants only; `resolveSlotState()` already treats power-ups and weapon drops as one shared loadout, so option A is a single flat list of at most six kinds plus slot-cap exemptions.

- **Q2 — Level format: how is the permanent level shown per row?**
  - A: Always show `Lv.N` on every row, including `Lv.1`. — **Recommended:** unambiguous and consistent with the adjacent offer labels (`"1.  Spread Shot Lv.3"`).
  - B: Show the level only when N ≥ 2 (`Spread Shot` alone at level 1).
  - C: Use the HUD's existing convention `Lvl N` (e.g. `Spread Shot Lvl 2`).
  - **Answer (Producer, interactive reply):** **A** — always show `Lv.N`, including `Lv.1`.
  - **Research:** the choice option names use `Lv.N` (`buildLevelUpOption`); the in-run HUD rows use `"<Name> Lvl <N>"` (`src/ui/HUD.ts`). Both conventions already ship, so either was defensible; the request only fixes *which* level (permanent) is shown, not the formatting.

- **Q3 — Presentation: heading and layout of the panel?**
  - A: One flat list under the heading `YOUR UPGRADES`, rows like `Spread Shot Lv.2`, and `YOUR UPGRADES — none yet` when nothing is permanently owned. — **Recommended:** minimum code that satisfies the request, and the names are self-explanatory.
  - B: Two grouped sections under the heading (`WEAPONS`, then `POWER-UPS`).
  - C: Flat list with slot usage in the heading (`YOUR UPGRADES 4/6`), tying the list to the six-slot cap (AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF).
  - **Answer (Producer, interactive reply):** **A** — one flat list under `YOUR UPGRADES`, with the `YOUR UPGRADES — none yet` empty state.
  - **Research:** the panel has the full top-left quadrant free (options occupy `y ≈ 200–420`, centred), and the six-slot cap bounds the list to ≤ 6 kinds, so all three options fit without scrolling. The empty state matters because the first hold-full of a run always occurs with zero permanent upgrades.

- **Non-blocking note — mini-boss reward overlay:** flagged that `openMiniBossReward()` reuses `MineralChoiceScene`; proposed default is hold-full launchers only. No objection recorded — implemented as the default (see Risks & assumptions).

- **Assumption — "hull full":** interpreted as the **hold-full mineral choice** overlay (the only permanent-choice list), consistent with AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR and AH-0MVLIJT3M005HPHF. No objection raised.
- **Assumption — no live refresh:** the panel reflects the state captured when the overlay opens; the overlay closes on selection, so no mid-overlay updates are required.

## Problem

`node_modules/.vite` accumulates orphaned `deps_temp_<hash>` directories whenever a Vite dep optimisation is interrupted or collides — at intake there were 98 (141 MB), now **95 dirs / 158 MB total in `node_modules/.vite`**. They are pure cache debris: each is a partially written pre-bundle. The epic's AC3 timing work is unaffected functionally, but the debris wastes disk, slows directory scans, and is evidence that dep optimisation is re-running/colliding (which is one source of the transform/import variance measured in AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG).

## Why this was not fixed inline

`node_modules` is **shared by every worktree on this host via symlink**; deleting the cache while another agent's suite is mid-run can corrupt that run. The producer rule 'never destroy another agent's work' applies, so the cleanup needs a safe, quiescent mechanism rather than an opportunistic `rm -rf`.

## Expected change

A small, documented, safe cleanup path — e.g. `scripts/clean-vite-cache.mjs` that:
- refuses to run when any `vitest`/`vite` process is alive (or requires `--force`),
- removes only `deps_temp_*` (never the valid `deps/` bundle or `deps_ssr`),
- reports bytes reclaimed, and
- is documented in `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` (cache-hygiene section) and optionally wired into `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A read-only `--dry-run` (default) reports the orphaned `deps_temp_*` count and bytes; `--apply` removes only those dirs and prints the reclaimed bytes.
- **AC2:** The script refuses to delete while a `vitest`/`vite` process is running unless `--force` is passed, and is covered by tests (dry-run classification, refusal path) that do not require a real cache.
- **AC3:** Documentation states why the cache is shared across worktrees and why the quiescence guard exists.
- **AC4:** After `--apply` on an idle host, `npx vitest run --project unit` still passes (cache regenerates cleanly).

## References

- AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG — measured the transform/import cost and rejected the optimizer/isolate/pool variants; notes the collision evidence.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — the existing periodic hygiene report this could extend.

# Align AI_Hell's test framework with the Tableau-Card-Engine game repos

AI_Hell runs a bespoke Vitest setup: `vitest.config.ts` + `vitest.projects.ts` with a
static classifier (`classifyTestFiles` / `isIntegrationTest` in `vitest.projects.ts`)
splitting test files into `unit` / `integration` projects, and test roots `src/`,
`scripts/`, `vite/` — there is **no top-level `tests/` directory**. Every sibling TCE
game repo (and the scaffold template `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) uses the
standard layout: a `unit` project in `vite.config.ts` with
`include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']` and no per-file classifier.

**Goal:** bring AI_Hell's test layout and project selection into line with the sibling
repos so cross-repo conventions, agent/audit tooling expectations (top-level `tests/`
tree), and the test skill's type profiles apply uniformly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No test lost or doubled.** After migration, AI_Hell's full suite runs the
   identical set of `*.test.ts` files currently selected by
   `vitest.projects.ts::allTestFiles` (src/, scripts/, vite/) — same count and same
   per-file project membership; verified by a before/after selection diff.
2. **Standard layout adopted.** Tests live under a top-level `tests/` tree laid out to
   match sibling repos (e.g. `tests/deploy/` for infra guards, `tests/<area>/`),
   selected via the standard include globs in `vitest.config.ts` (or the config file's
   `test.projects`), with `tsconfig.json` including `tests/**/*.ts`.
3. **Isolation preserved.** Phaser/DOM-booting tests retain their separation from the
   fast node `unit` project (the deliberate unit/integration split — parent
   AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV, blocked child AH-0MVF6XV87001NSEJ). Alignment must NOT flatten
   Phaser-heavy tests into the node unit project or regress suite runtime. The
   `src/test/projectMembership.test.ts` guard is updated to assert the new layout and
   still passes.
4. **Tooling keeps working.** The test skill's per-type profiles
   (`.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`, `.pi/test-config.json`) remain
   functional — update only if project names/commands change, and verify each type
   (`unit`, `coverage`, `e2e`) runs.
5. **Documentation updated.** Comments in the vitest config(s), AGENTS.md and any
   dev notes reflect the new layout. CHANGELOG.md excluded (ship skill).
6. **Full suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- Refactor only — no change to app behaviour.
- Preserve the deterministic membership guard pattern (`vitest.projects.ts` is
  deliberately the single source of truth for selection; keep an equivalent guard).
- This item may also relocate `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` (added by the watch-ignore
  port, MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0) into `tests/deploy/` for full parity — sequence after or
  alongside that port.

## Related work

- MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0 — Port Vite watcher-ignore to sibling game repos (discovering item; adds `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` under the current layout)
- AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV — parent of the unit/integration split decision
- AH-0MVF6XV87001NSEJ — Unit/integration Vitest project split (blocked)
- AH-0MV53ABBU008FKE0 — Test-skill runner no-ops: no .pi/test-config.json suiteCommands for vitest (completed)

# UFO Feel — Intake brief (final, producer answers incorporated)

**FINAL DRAFT** — producer answered Q1=B, Q2=C, Q3=A (see Appendix).
Stage to follow: intake_complete (via intake finish + coverage review).

## Problem statement

The Mystery UFO collector drone flies, harvests and dies **silently and
without feedback**: it has no visual effects and no sounds for any lifecycle
moment, so the reward reads as dead game feel. We need the classic Space
Invaders mystery-ship juice: a "woo-woo-woo" UFO warble while it is deployed,
a reward cue when it returns to the player, and an explosion plus a "tinkle" of
dropped resources when it is destroyed — with full-juice VFX at every lifecycle
stage.

## Users

- **Player** (the primary stakeholder) — wants the Mystery UFO to *feel* like
  the Space Invaders homage it is: an audible, celebratory arcade reward with
  visible juice at spawn, on collect, on return and on death.
- **Developer / quality gates** — wants the juice to run through the existing
  ToneForge audio pipeline and shared VFX so the game and every gym stay
  identical (gym↔game parity).

### Example user stories

- As a player, I want to hear the classic UFO warble for the drone's whole
  sortie so I always know it is out there farming for me.
- As a player, I want to see the saucer come alive (running-light pulse, a poof
  on launch, sparkles as it vacuums, a trail on the way home) so the drone
  reads as a living reward.
- As a player, I want a reward fanfare when the drone flies home and pays out
  so the economic payoff feels earned.
- As a player, I want a satisfying explosion and the tinkle of minerals
  scattering when an enemy shoots the drone down, so the loss/opportunity
  reads clearly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Warble loop (Q2=C).** A classic "woo-woo-woo" UFO warble cue plays continuously from spawn through the **seek and collect** phases (the whole sortie) and stops when the drone begins its return leg, pays out, is destroyed, or is torn down — delivered as a start/stop continuous cue with control companions (mirroring `stopDiveSound`/`stopThrusterSound`), at a level-appropriate audible gain that respects the shared SFX volume/mute settings.
2. **Reward cue (Q3=A).** A distinct reward fanfare plays on **arrival at the player**, synchronised with the hold pay-in (exactly when `MysteryUfoDrone._payOut` credits the sink), so the payout moment is audible.
3. **Destruction feedback.** On enemy destruction the drone plays an explosion cue **and** spawns the explosion particle VFX at the crash site (reusing `src/vfx/explosionParticles.ts`); a mineral "tinkle" cue fires in sync with the spilled resource drops (spill already exists via `hitDrone`/`scatterMineralDrops`), so the dropped minerals read audibly.
4. **Full-juice VFX (Q1=B).** Code-drawn Phaser graphics (no external art) add the full lifecycle juice: spawn poof at launch, per-mineral collect sparkle/ring while vacuuming, a running-light pulse animation on the saucer rim, and a return-leg trail/glow — all in addition to the destruction explosion VFX.
5. **Pipeline, parity & quality.** Every new cue is a baked ToneForge delivery (recipe YAMLs under `audio/toneforge/recipes/`, entries in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`, wrappers in `src/audio/effects.ts`, WAVs rendered via `npm run build-audio`); the cue-manifest / effects-contract / build-audio / audio-balance-guard suites pass; the continuous warble has start/stop control lifecycle and every cue degrades to a safe no-op without an AudioContext; the VFX/SFX run through shared core so `PlayScene` and the gym scenes are identical (duplicate-body guard + gym-parity docs assertion pass, `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` green); the full project test suite passes and relevant docs (GDD §7.3 / Mystery UFO section, `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`) are updated.

## Constraints

- Audio must flow through the existing ToneForge pipeline — no new external
  assets (procedural WAV baked at build time; `file:../ToneForge` dependency).
- The continuous warble requires start/stop control lifecycle (`ControlCues` in
  the manifest) and must respect the shared SFX volume/mute settings.
- VFX must be code-drawn Phaser graphics (repo convention: no external art).
- Every cue must be a safe no-op without an `AudioContext` (headless tests and
  autoplay-blocked browsers) — the effects contract suite enforces this.
- Behaviour must live once in shared core (`src/scenes/core/`) and be consumed
  by both the game and the gyms (gym↔game parity, AGENTS.md).
- Peak-volume/balance guarded by `scripts/audio-balance-guard.mjs`.

## Existing state

- `MysteryUfoDrone` (src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts) is a pure entity with a
  code-drawn saucer (running lights, dome, glow) but **zero VFX/SFX**: no cue is
  called anywhere in the drone, the shared pass (`src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts`),
  or the spawn path. Collection (`_vacuum`) hides minerals with no feedback;
  destruction (`_destroyByEnemy` + `hitDrone`) already spills minerals via
  `scatterMineralDrops` but with no explosion/tinkle feedback.
- The audio pipeline is ToneForge-baked: `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` maps
  every cue to a recipe; `src/audio/effects.ts` exports thin playback wrappers;
  WAVs are baked by `npm run build-audio`. No UFO cue exists yet.

## Desired change

Add the "feel" layer so every Mystery UFO lifecycle moment gives feedback
through the shared pipeline, identically in the game and the gyms: warble for
the whole sortie, a reward fanfare on payout, explosion + mineral tinkle +
particle burst on destruction, plus the full-juice VFX set (spawn poof, collect
sparkle, running-light pulse, return trail).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts` — lifecycle state hooks (spawn, collect,
  return, payout, destroyed) driving the SFX/VFX seams; running-light pulse
  animation in the saucer draw/update.
- `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts` — shared tick/spawn/destroy pass: warble
  start/stop in `tickDrones`, destruction explosion + tinkle adjacent to the
  existing spill in `hitDrone`, spawn poof in `spawnDrone`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` / `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` /
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — shared wiring so game and gyms run the same code.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — new cue wrappers: warble loop + `stopMysteryUfoWarbleSound`
  control companion, `playMysteryUfoRewardSound`, `playMysteryUfoDestroySound`,
  `playMineralTinkleSound`.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — new cue→recipe entries (+ control cue).
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/*.yaml` — new `aihell-mystery-ufo-*` recipes
  (warble, reward, destroy, mineral tinkle).
- `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` / `src/audio/sfxPlayback.ts` / `src/audio/cueVoiceLimiter.ts`
  — continuous-cue start/stop plumbing for the warble.
- `src/vfx/` — spawn poof, collect sparkle/ring, return trail (small new/module
  effects, following `explosionParticles.ts` conventions); `explosionParticles.ts`
  reused for the destruction burst.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§7.3 + Mystery UFO section),
  `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — documentation updates.

## Related work

- **AH-0MV9G113S009B37I** — Mystery UFO has no visible representation (epic,
  completed): the collector-drone entity and shared pass this item adds feel to.
- **AH-0MVH7ZC5N003JS92** — Mystery UFO needs a better graphical representation
  (completed): the code-drawn saucer VFX baseline this item animates.
- **AH-0MV1BIXFO006Z1I7** — Space Invaders mystery UFO bonus (completed): the
  classic reference the warble/reward homage draws from.
- **AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J** — Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to
  ToneForge (epic): the pipeline every new cue must flow through.
- **AH-0MVBMPZ2C0008VAE** — Drone level variables and curve specs (completed).
- **AH-0MVBMQ0HR0064THH** — Gym parity for the collector drone (completed).

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: **VFX scope.** "The item says the Mystery UFO currently has no VFX or
  SFX but does not specify which visual effects to add. (a) Minimal...; (b)
  Full juice — also add spawn poof, return-trail/glow, running-light pulse;
  (c) Sound-only."
  — Answer (producer, via review reply "1. B (with SFX)"): **B — full juice**,
  with the SFX set confirmed in scope alongside the VFX. Source: producer
  review reply on AH-0MVI4J8R4002WTT6 (comment thread
  AH-C0MVNZ64M5000W4NL). Final AC 4 (full-juice VFX) + ACs 1–3 (SFX) reflect
  this.
- Q2: **"woo-woo-woo" delivery.** "(a) continuous looping cue while the drone
  is in the collect phase; (b) discrete one-shot per collected mineral; (c) a
  looping cue that plays for the whole sortie (seek+collect)."
  — Answer (producer, "2. C"): **C — loop for the whole sortie** (seek +
  collect), so the warble starts at spawn and ends at return/payout/destruction.
  Source: producer review reply. Final AC 1 reflects this.
- Q3: **Reward timing.** "(a) on arrival at the ship, synchronised with the
  payout pay-in; (b) when the drone begins the return leg; (c) both."
  — Answer (producer, "3. A"): **A — on arrival/payout**, synced with the hold
  credit. Source: producer review reply. Final AC 2 reflects this.

### Assumptions (documented)

- The original description's "no VFX or VFX" is a typo for "no VFX or SFX"
  (confirmed implicitly by Q1 answer B *with SFX*).
- Level progression (lifetime/capacity/radius) does **not** change the sound
  character — same cues at every level (no per-level variant recipes).
- New cues respect the existing volume balance budget (≤ ~0.2 peak per layer,
  `audio-balance-guard`) and the global SFX mute/volume settings automatically
  via the shared playback provider.
- Running-light pulse is a static-free animation of the existing
  code-drawn lights (alpha/colour oscillation), not a new emitter.

### Risks

- **Audio-pipeline risk (med).** Every new cue is a build-time WAV bake: recipe
  YAML, manifest entry, wrapper and `npm run build-audio` render must stay in
  lock-step or the contract suites (cue-manifest / effects-contract /
  build-audio / audio-balance-guard) fail red. Mitigation: follow the exact
  pattern of an existing baked cue (e.g. `aihell-diver-dive-loop`) end to end.
- **Continuous-cue lifecycle risk (med).** The sortie-long warble must start
  exactly once at spawn and stop on every terminal path (return, payout,
  destroyed, teardown) or it will leak a looping voice. Mitigation: start/stop
  via the shared control-companion pattern (`ControlCues`) and asset in
  `tickDrones` where removal is final; extend the cue-contract test to assert
  stop-on-all-terminals.
- **Collect-sparkle VFX performance (low-med).** At the max collector radius
  (40 px) a drone can vacuum several minerals in one tick; a sparkle per
  mineral must be small, short-lived and capped, not an unbounded emitter.
  Mitigation: reuse `explosionParticles`-style pooled graphics and cap per-tick
  spawns.
- **Parity risk (med).** If a gym or `PlayScene` wires the SFX/VFX outside the
  shared core, the duplicate-body guard / gym-parity docs assertion fail and
  the game and gyms drift. Mitigation: implement through
  `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts` and shared hooks only (AGENTS.md
  architecture convention).
- **Scope-creep risk (med).** The chosen full-juice VFX set (poof, sparkle,
  pulse, trail) is wide for one item. Extra polish discovered during
  implementation (e.g. pay-in burst on the ship, level-scaled bloom) must be
  recorded as new work items, not absorbed into this one.

### Duplicate-work check

Performed `wl search "UFO"` / `"woo"` / `"mystery ufo vfx"` — completed items
cover visual representation (AH-0MVH7ZC5N003JS92), visibility epic
(AH-0MV9G113S009B37I) and the classic reference (AH-0MV1BIXFO006Z1I7); **no
overlapping item for UFO audio/VFX feel exists**. No duplicate — proceed.
---

## Plan: changelog (plan skill, AH-0MVI4J8R4002WTT6)

- **2026-10-28** — Planned via /skill:plan. Pre-check `plan-if-needed` → `plan` (Small/Medium); plan-approval-gate → `request_approval: false` (no approval pause). Created 6 child items (test-first): UFO feel test seams, ToneForge UFO cue bake, Sortie warble lifecycle, Terminal reward and destruction feedback, Saucer lifecycle VFX juice, UFO feel docs and quality gate. Deps wired (test seams + cue bake → warble → terminal feedback; VFX → docs/gate). Parent AC section unwrapped to single lines so AC coverage is machine-comparable (formatting only). Six automated review stages run; AC coverage review → `proceed` (all 5 parent ACs covered). Parent stage → `plan_complete`. Effort/risk reused from existing estimate (Small / Medium, comment AH-C0MVNZHO3W000ZBLP) — not re-estimated.

### Appendix addition (planning run)

- Q: "Did planning need any further clarifying questions from the producer?" — Answer (this run): No new questions. All three design decisions were already resolved in intake (Q1=B full juice, Q2=C whole-sortie warble, Q3=A arrival/payout, recorded above), the effort/risk estimate is on file, and the plan-approval gate requested no approval. Planning proceeded from the intake brief's Acceptance Criteria directly.

# Intake Brief: Promo video scenarios (10+)

**Priority:** medium · **Issue type:** feature · **Assignee:** Map
**Status:** CONFIRMED — producer answered Q1 (b), Q2 (c), Q3 (a) on AH-0MVI5XI73000ZVYA.

## Problem statement

The game can record bot-flown gameplay clips (`npm run capture`) and compile
them into a promo, showreel and highlights (`compile-promo`), and the footage
can only show what the current run happens to contain. Today the only dev
scenarios are capture shortcuts (`boss`, `boss-four-hits`, `defeat`) that jump
to an already-terminal boss fight; there is no curated set of scenes that
showcases the game's range. A promo video therefore needs dedicated,
reproducible scenarios — each pairing an interesting ship configuration with a
deliberate enemy wave — that the Watch Demo and the capture tooling can drive
on demand.

## Users

- **Producer / marketing** — wants a selection of visually distinct, reliably
  capturable moments to assemble into a promo video without hand-playing runs.
- **Player of Watch Demo** — sees varied, interesting bot-flown gameplay in the
  attract loop rather than the same default run each time.

### Example user stories

- As a producer, I want to record a boss battle, a pick-up frenzy and a dense
  enemy horde from fixed, reproducible scenarios so the promo covers each
  editorial category.
- As a player, I want the Watch Demo to fly a variety of bot/loadout and enemy
  combinations so the attract loop shows off the game's range.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 (ten scenarios):** At least 10 scenarios are registered in the shared
  registry (`scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`) and resolvable via the existing
  `scenario` URL query parameter, dev-gated behind `import.meta.env.DEV`
  exactly like today's scenarios — a production build and a normal run are
  unchanged.
- **AC2 (composition):** Every scenario starts from (i) the **single shipped
  ship config** paired with a **curated bot-tuning preset** in `src/data/
  bot-tuning.json` (optionally a starting weapon/loadout where existing
  mechanics support it) and (ii) a **hand-authored promo wave definition**
  composed from the existing spawner/movement machinery; each scenario is
  deterministic for a given seed and **bot-pilotable end to end**, sustaining
  enough watchable footage for a promo cut (target ≥45 s of action before the
  demo game-over dwell).
- **AC3 (range):** The scenario set evidences every promo editorial category
  from `EDITORIAL_CONFIG` (`weapons`, `pickups`, `enemies`, `boss`) with at
  least one scenario each, and the set is ordered to open with a high
  action-intensity hook so the first captured cut has no dead air.
- **AC4 (capture integration):** `npm run capture -- --list-scenarios` lists
  every scenario with its one-line effect, and `npm run capture --
  --all-scenarios` records one clean clip per scenario.
- **AC5 (tests):** Hermetic tests pin registry ↔ resolver parity, each
  scenario's bot-tuning preset and wave definition, and dev-only gating; an
  integration/demo check confirms a scenario is flown by the Watch Demo bot.
- **AC6 (docs):** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, capture `--help` and
  `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`.
- **AC7 (suite):** The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Scenarios are **dev-only**: gated behind `import.meta.env.DEV` exactly like
  today's scenarios (`src/core/devScenario.ts`); the shipped bundle stays
  inert.
- Single source of truth remains `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`; the game
  resolver and the capture CLI must not drift (registry ↔ resolver parity
  test enforced).
- Scenarios are **bot-flown** (the Watch Demo bot / competent bot), reproducible
  per seed, and must not require a human pilot to produce good footage.
- **Wave definitions are new hand-authored content**, but must be composed from
  the **existing spawner/movement machinery** (V/diver swarm, centipede, ghost,
  harvester, horde, strike, lane traffic, asteroid, boss/minion classes) — no
  new gameplay behaviour, so the gym↔game parity and duplicate-body guards in
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` are not triggered.
- The shipped ship config (`ship-config.csv`) is **unchanged**; variety comes
  from bot-tuning presets and loadouts, not new ship rows.

## Existing state

- Ship configs: **one** row in `src/data/ship-config.csv` (asteroids scheme,
  thrust 300 px/s², maxSpeed 175 px/s). ShipConfig shape: `configTypes.ts:372`.
- Bot tuning: named presets via `src/core/botTuningStore.ts`, persisted in
  `src/data/bot-tuning.json` (currently one `Default` preset with `competent`
  + `human` layers); Watch Demo flies the current preset
  (AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL).
- Waves: static `LEVELS` (`src/waves/Formations.ts`), data-driven difficulty
  curves (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv`) sequenced by
  `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts`; spawners per movement class in `src/waves/`.
- Power-ups/weapons: 16 power-up ids and 12 weapon drop ids
  (`src/powerups/types.ts`).
- Scenario infra: registry `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` (3 entries),
  resolver `src/core/devScenario.ts`, capture CLI `--scenario /
  --list-scenarios / --all-scenarios`, page-side handle
  `window.__aiHellScenario` to release frozen runs.

## Desired change

Extend the dev-scenario registry so each entry carries the **bot-tuning preset
name** (and optional start loadout) plus its **hand-authored wave definition**
and optional seed. A new promo-wave module (`src/waves/promoScenarios.*`
naming TBD at implementation) hosts the hand-authored definitions, each built
from the existing spawner classes; the scenario resolver applies them at run
start through the existing seams (ship config loading, bot-tuning application,
wave sequencing, run seeding) rather than adding new gameplay. The result is a
catalogue of ≥10 named, documented promo scenarios driveable by
`npm run capture -- --scenario <name>` and the Watch Demo, covering all four
editorial categories and ordered to open with a high-intensity hook.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs` — extend registry entries with bot-tuning
  preset + wave definition + optional loadout/seed metadata.
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.d.mts` — types for the richer entries.
- `src/core/devScenario.ts` — resolve and apply the preset and wave at run
  start; extend the resolved-scenario union.
- `src/core/botTuningStore.ts` / `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — curated presets
  per scenario (Q1 answer: single ship, varied presets).
- `src/waves/` — new hand-authored promo wave definitions reusing existing
  spawner/movement classes, with tests (Q2 answer).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — scenario application seam at run start.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `--help`, README — documentation (AC6).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** scenarios are surfaced via the existing registry/URL-param
  pattern plus the capture CLI — no new menu picker unless requested (scope
  creep risk if a visible picker is added later; record as a separate item).
- **Assumption (Q1):** "interesting ship configuration" is delivered through
  bot-tuning/loadout variety on the single shipped ship — no new ShipConfig
  rows. Loadout variety limited to what existing mechanics support.
- **Assumption (Q2):** hand-authored waves live in a new dev-gated module
  composed from existing spawners — content, not new behaviour.
- **Risk:** hand-authored waves must be calibrated so the competent bot
  survives and keeps collecting — a scenario the bot dies in instantly is a
  wasted clip; the ≥45 s sustained-footage target implies some scenarios span
  several waves with the demo game-over dwell only at the end.
- **Risk:** promo footage reads as repetitive if the wave set is a flat list of
  similar archetypes — AC3's category mapping and an intense opening mitigate.
- **Scope-creep risk:** an attract-mode playlist / menu picker for these
  scenarios is out of scope for this item; create a linked follow-up if wanted.

## Related work

- AH-0MV6JGE9R005YOL1 Shared scenario registry and contract tests (completed)
- AH-0MUZM8ATZ002AKFP Batch scenario listing and multi-video capture (completed)
- AH-0MV6JGQFK007MXGX Add --all-scenarios batch capture (completed)
- AH-0MVDV4RJ300459ZF Editorial config and feature-coverage manifest (completed)
- AH-0MVDV4OKN001OT18 Implement: pure edit-plan and selection logic in compile-promo (completed)
- AH-0MVDV50Z20071RF4 Produce and validate the promo, showreel and highlight clips (completed)
- AH-0MV6MFDYG001E6PL Watch Demo and video recording should fly the saved bot-tuning configuration (completed)
- AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2 Add 5 new levels before the boss showcasing the classic-arcade enemy roster (completed)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Ship configurations: only one ShipConfig exists today. Where should the
  'interesting ship configuration' per scenario come from? (a) Author 2–4
  additional ShipConfig rows; (b) Keep the single ship; vary the
  bot-tuning/loadout preset instead; (c) Both." —
  **Answer (producer): (b) Keep the single ship; vary the bot-tuning/loadout
  preset instead.** Source: interactive reply on the work item, 2026-10-27.
  Research: `src/data/ship-config.csv` has one row; `botTuningStore` supports
  named presets (`bot-tuning.json`); Watch Demo already flies the current
  preset. Final ACs reflect preset/loadout variety, no new ship rows.
- Q2: "Enemy waves: where do the waves come from? (a) Reuse existing campaign
  content plus a few hand-authored waves; (b) Reuse existing content only;
  (c) Hand-author all new promo-tailored wave definitions." —
  **Answer (producer): (c) Hand-author all new promo-tailored wave
  definitions.** Source: interactive reply on the work item, 2026-10-27.
  Research: spawner/movement classes exist per archetype in `src/waves/`;
  hand-authored definitions reuse them, keeping the parity guards quiet.
- Q3: "'Wide range of experiences': how should the 10+ scenarios be defined?
  (a) Map across the promo editorial categories (weapons, pickups, enemies,
  boss), open with a high-intensity hook; (b) Showcase specific enemy
  archetypes without category mapping; (c) Simplest 10+ slots." —
  **Answer (producer): (a) Map across editorial categories; open with a high
  action-intensity hook.** Source: interactive reply on the work item,
  2026-10-27. Research: `EDITORIAL_CONFIG.categories` in
  `scripts/compile-promo.mjs`; the coverage manifest requires every category
  to be evidenced.
